title: How to compare car insurance quotes without comparing apples to oranges
description: A practical checklist for matching limits, deductibles and optional coverages before judging price.

sections.heading: Match liability limits first
sections.text: Two quotes are not comparable when one carries lower bodily injury or property damage limits. Put every quote on the same liability structure before comparing the premium.

sections.heading: Normalize deductibles
sections.text: Collision and comprehensive deductibles can materially change price. Compare the same deductible whenever possible and note whether glass coverage or special deductibles differ.

sections.heading: Check what is missing
sections.text: Uninsured motorist, rental reimbursement, roadside assistance, gap coverage and new-car replacement can change the value of a policy. A lower premium can simply mean fewer protections.

title: Replacement cost vs. market value: the home insurance distinction that changes your quote
description: Why dwelling coverage should be compared on rebuilding cost rather than the price you could sell the property for.

sections.heading: Market value is not rebuilding cost
sections.text: Land value, neighborhood demand and transaction prices do not equal the cost of rebuilding the structure after a covered loss.

sections.heading: Review coverage assumptions
sections.text: Construction type, square footage, local labor and material costs, special features and code requirements can all affect a replacement-cost estimate.

sections.heading: Watch percentage deductibles
sections.text: Some wind, hurricane or catastrophe deductibles are expressed as a percentage of insured value rather than a flat dollar amount. That can materially change out-of-pocket exposure.

title: Term life insurance quote checklist: what to compare before price
description: Term length, coverage amount, underwriting and policy features that matter before choosing the cheapest offer.

sections.heading: Keep coverage amount and term identical
sections.text: A 20-year policy and a 30-year policy are different products. Compare quotes only when term length and death benefit match.

sections.heading: Understand underwriting
sections.text: Accelerated, simplified and fully underwritten policies can price risk differently. The fastest application is not always the least expensive long-term option.

sections.heading: Read conversion and rider provisions
sections.text: Conversion rights and optional riders can matter later. Compare them explicitly instead of treating every term policy as interchangeable.

title: Renters insurance: the 5 coverages worth checking before you buy
description: Personal property, liability, loss of use and deductible details that make inexpensive renters policies meaningfully different.

sections.heading: Personal property valuation
sections.text: Know whether damaged belongings are paid at replacement cost or actual cash value, which can deduct depreciation.

sections.heading: Liability protection
sections.text: Liability limits can matter far more than the value of your furniture if someone is injured and you are legally responsible.

sections.heading: Loss of use
sections.text: Temporary housing and additional living expense coverage can be crucial when a covered loss makes the rental uninhabitable.

title: Small-business insurance: where to start before requesting quotes
description: A coverage map for general liability, property, professional liability, cyber, workers compensation and commercial auto.

sections.heading: Start from the actual risk
sections.text: A consultant, restaurant, contractor and ecommerce company have very different exposures. Coverage should follow operations rather than a generic bundle.

sections.heading: Separate liability types
sections.text: General liability, professional liability and cyber liability address different categories of loss. One is not automatically a substitute for another.

sections.heading: Confirm compulsory coverages
sections.text: Workers compensation, commercial auto and other requirements vary by jurisdiction. Verify obligations with the relevant regulator or licensed professional.

title: Health insurance: compare total cost, not just the monthly premium
description: A framework for evaluating deductibles, copays, coinsurance, networks and out-of-pocket maximums.

sections.heading: Premium is only one cost
sections.text: A plan with a low monthly premium can still expose you to a high deductible or out-of-pocket maximum.

sections.heading: Check the network
sections.text: Doctors, hospitals and pharmacies may be treated differently in-network and out-of-network. Verify the providers that matter to you.

sections.heading: Model likely use
sections.text: Consider regular prescriptions, specialist visits, planned procedures and worst-case annual exposure rather than optimizing one number.
